text: Full Zelle feature set (send, request, Split, QR, Zelle tag, scheduled sends) with explicit reimbursement language for unauthorized transactions and 'certain qualifying imposter scams' in Citi's own T&Cs [S001].

Citibank Global Transfers: no transfer fee for Citi-to-Citi transfers in the U.S. and select countries (FX commission embedded in the rate for foreign currency), funds moved once the transfer is reviewed; an on-us cross-border rail (peer comparison to be confirmed in the cross-bank synthesis) [S903].
RTP pioneer: participant since 2017; first U.S. bank to receive, display and pay Request-for-Payment e-bills (Sept 2021); TTS offers end-to-end RfP origination [S026, S027].

CitiBusiness Online has a deep control framework: per-account entitlements, tiered co-signing approvals, Maker-Checker, Secured Wires, wire models, batch dual approval, and mobile soft-token approvals with push notifications [S009, S010, S021].
Comprehensive legal terms for online wires and remittances (30-minute cancellation, 180-day error window, same-day rejection email) and a 'Pay Bills' late-fee promise [S016, S002].

Public IIT page now discloses same-day ACH (requests before 12:30 PM ET) and tenured/untenured limits (inbound up to $100,000/day), with the review screen showing an estimated deposit date [S902][S912].

Citi Online money-movement screens are consolidated under a 'Payments Dashboard' with 'Manage Payees and Bills' / 'Manage Bills & Payees', a unified 'Transfer Between Your Accounts' page and 'View/Manage Activity' / 'All Transfer Activity' views [S912].

Intra Citi Transfers became fee-free for all tiers on November 8, 2025 [S911]; Citibank Global Transfers remain fee-free with a simple four-field 'Add a CGT Payee' set-up and weekly limits up to $500,000 for Citigold Private Client [S903][S912].
Mobile Check Deposit sends two-stage confirmation emails (received, accepted) and has a dedicated support line [S905].
Restricted Access terms (Apr 2026) explicitly let Citi block, delay or return transfers and hold funds when it suspects the customer is a scam victim — a protective control for APP fraud [S911].
Small-business ACH Origination requires Maker/Checker dual control (two unique users) for every new enrollment [S907][S908].

citi.com product pages for Zelle, transfers, wires, bill pay, Global Transfers and mobile deposit are JavaScript shells with no crawlable content; exact in-app navigation labels, scam interstitial copy and status states cannot be verified publicly.
IIT external-account verification method is not disclosed (accounts are only 'verified'); cancelling one transfer in a series cancels all subsequent transfers to that external account [S911][S902].

No evidence of consumer-initiated RTP/FedNow send or a bank-initiated instant push-to-debit-card product; debit-card P2P is passive acceptance inside third-party apps (send limit raised to $2,500/day effective Sept 19, 2026) [S911].
eBills/autopay mechanics are undocumented (legacy 'Ebill' page now redirects); Citi Mobile App 'bill management' is flagged limited availability [S045, S018].

CitiBusiness Online retains a legacy navigation vocabulary ('Main Menu > Transfers and Payments') and business Zelle sits outside CBOL approvals; two separate business digital channels (CBOL vs. Citibank Online for Small Business).

IIT external-account verification method is still undisclosed; the IIT Terms and Conditions link on the product page opens an empty modal, and the page tells customers to migrate to a new 'Transfer Between Your Accounts' service without explaining it [S902].
No digital intake for deposit-account EFT/scam claims: ATM/Debit and Zelle/ACH/wire problems go to Chat or phone, whereas credit cards have an in-app Dispute Center [S912][S913].
App-store release notes for every 2025-2026 Citi Mobile version are identical boilerplate, giving customers no visibility into money-movement changes [S909][S910].
Online wire fees rise on August 1, 2026 ($30 Standard / $25 Priority domestic; $40 / $35 international USD) [S911].
eBills exist but their enrollment and auto-pay mechanics are not documented anywhere public; bill-pay marketing page omits eBills entirely [S904][S912].
The Global Transfers destination-country list link does not render [S903].

NY AG v. Citibank (S.D.N.Y. 24-cv-659): alleged notarized-affidavit prerequisite, account lock + branch visit, pro-forma investigations with 30-60 day form-letter denials for unauthorized online wires; CFPB complaints about Citi's wire-fraud handling 'nearly tripled from 2020 to 2022' (allegations; Op. pp. 2-6) [S965].
Citibank Global Transfer Service (on-us cross-border, free).
RTP Request-for-Payment e-bill receipt for retail customers.
Tenure-based ('untenured'/'tenured') Zelle limit model disclosed in T&Cs.
CitiBusiness Mobile Token replacing hard tokens for CBOL login and wire approval.
Online funds-transfer terms explicitly addressing third-party AI agents (customer bears responsibility) [S016].
Tenure-based limits (91-day rule) applied consistently across Zelle and Inter-Institution Transfers [S902][S916].
In-app Direct Deposit enrollment with payer search ('Search and select your payer from the list') tied to the Enhanced Direct Deposit fee-waiver programme [S906].
Consumer Deposit Account Agreement names an 'Instant Payment Service' as a consumer EFT service — a possible precursor to consumer instant send [S911].
Citi joined FedNow in 2025 [S024] and appears on the Federal Reserve live-participant list (as of Nov 2, 2026), so it can at least receive; send capability unconfirmed [S951].

Consumer Deposit Account Agreement effective Nov 20, 2025 now names 'Instant Payments, Real Time Payments' among qualifying New-to-Citibank Funds [S028]; CitiBusiness Client Manual updated Nov 11, 2025 [S029].
Paze online checkout extended to eligible Citi credit cardmembers (March 2026) [S022].
CitiBusiness Mobile added push notifications (Aug 2025) and security enhancements (Sept 2025) [S021]; Citi Mobile app at v9.100.0 (Nov 2026) [S018].
Zelle network fact sheet (Jan 2026) reiterates mandatory pre-send in-app alerts and imposter-scam reimbursement [S020]; Citi's Zelle T&Cs mirror this.
Citi Services: 24/7 USD clearing (~300 banks), Citi Express instant payments in 22 markets, partnerships with Mastercard, Coinbase and Dandelion [S024].
Nov 8, 2025: Intra Citi Transfer fees waived for all tiers (CDAA amendment) [S911].
Dec 5, 2025: Citibank ATM deposit limits — $20,000 cash per rolling 30 days and 5 checks per card per 24 hours [S911].
Dec 31, 2025: 'Emergency Cash' service discontinued (CDAA Appendix 3) [S911].
Jan 26, 2026: Safety Check Transfers terms replaced [S911].
Apr 1, 2026: 'Restricted Access' terms rewritten to cover blocking/holding transfers for suspected scam victims and mismatched incoming credits [S911].
Jul 18, 2026: 'Enhanced Direct Deposit' definition retired in favour of 'Direct Deposits or other qualifying transactions' [S911][S906].
Aug 1, 2026: Online domestic/international USD wire fees increased to $30/$40 Standard ($25/$35 Citi Priority) [S911].
Sep 19, 2026: Debit-card person-to-person send limit raised from $1,000 to $2,500 per day across all tiers [S911].
Jan 1, 2027: Regular Checking fee-waiver threshold rises to $1,000/month in Direct Deposits or other qualifying transactions [S906][S911].

Citi Mobile App releases roughly monthly (9.90.0 Nov 13, 2025 -> iOS 9.100.0, App Store listing dated early Nov 2026; Google Play updated Oct 28, 2026) with boilerplate notes [S909][S910]; citi.com login offers 'Passwordless Sign On' [S901].
Sept 28, 2026: Citi Token Services expands to Japan and UAE; live in 7 markets including the United States (institutional) [S952].
Sept 29, 2026: Citi first bank live with multiple markets on the Swift payments scheme via WorldLink/Global Clearing (AUD, GBP, INR, USD; real-time USD credits to Citi U.S. account holders) [S953].
Nov 2026: Online Funds Transfer terms updated to make customers solely responsible for instructions given by third-party AI agents [S016].

Jan 21, 2025: S.D.N.Y. held EFTA can apply to fraudulent online consumer payment orders funded by account debit; Mar 25, 2025: CFPB withdrew its statement of interest; 2025: 2d Cir. accepted interlocutory appeal (No. 25-2105), argument Apr 6, 2026, decision pending as of Nov 2026 [S965].
Nacha Phase 1/2 fraud-monitoring rules effective Mar 20 / Jun 19, 2026 [S969].

Mobile Check Deposit limits, endorsement wording and hold schedule (Appendix 2 not retrievable).
Current eBills/autopay flow and biller roster for RfP e-bills.

IIT external-account verification method remains undisclosed (only 'subject to verification by Citibank'); the IIT T&C modal is empty.
Mobile Check Deposit limits, endorsement wording and hold schedule live in a separate MCD agreement that is not public (CDAA Appendix 2 defers to it).
eBill enrollment flow, biller roster and auto-pay of eBills (only 'unfile an eBill' FAQ exists).
What the new 'Transfer Between Your Accounts' service changes versus legacy IIT (e.g., instant verification, faster delivery).
Exact release date of Citi Mobile iOS 9.100.0 (App Store shows early Nov 2026 vs Oct 27-28, 2026 elsewhere); a dated version-history capture would settle it (CITI-C012).
Current consumer statement labels for debit-card P2P credits/debits (2017 insert said 'MoneySend Credit/Debit'; current CDAA silent).
If the 2d Cir. affirms, Citi (and peers) would need Reg E error-resolution (provisional credit, 10/45-day timelines) for online consumer wires; has Citi changed its affidavit requirement? [S965]
Does the mainline CDAA (eff. Nov 20, 2025) Sections 8-9 repeat the Alliance 6.3 written-confirmation rule, and what is the 'Instant Payment Service' (undefined in both CDAA_CA 6.1 and CDAA 8.1)?

Is the 'Immediate Funds Transfers (both international and domestic)' row in the Online Funds Transfer T&C availability table (S980) the same thing as the CDAA 'Instant Payment Service', and on which rail does it settle?
